Sofia (People Ops): FYI — offer accepted for Priya (Data Engineer) but she needs to travel to India for a family emergency next week. She’s currently on OPT and we were planning to file H-1 COS later this quarter. Can we discuss start-date flexibility and benefits timing?
Aisha (Recruiter): Oh no — hope all ok. She said travel is 7–10 days max, but might be delayed by passport renewal at local passport office. Wants to start remotely if possible.
Kunal (Benefits): Quick Q: if she starts remote before COS is filed, can we enroll her in benefits on day 1 or do we need proof of work authorization?
Miguel (Payroll): Payroll needs completed I-9 and tax forms. Remote onboarding is fine but I-9 needs either in-person verification or a notary workaround for international hires.
Immigration-Counsel-Bot: Per counsel: OPT holders can continue work for employer during authorized OPT. Travel while OPT is risky if visa stamping needed, but short domestic travel (to India) may complicate re-entry depending on consulate delays. COS filing can be done while she’s in US — but if she leaves before approval, COS may be affected. Recommend delaying travel until after biometrics (if required) OR file premium for H-1 if timeline tight.
Alex (Hiring Manager): From team perspective, we can onboard her remotely and give access to code and Slack on day 1. We need her to attend onboarding calls in PST. No customer-facing tasks first week.
Sofia (People Ops): Proposed options: 1) Keep original start date, allow remote onboarding, enroll benefits based on offer start and then adjust if docs delayed. 2) Push start 2 weeks and do full in-person I-9 when she returns. Need input from benefits and payroll.
Kunal (Benefits): We can provisionally enroll on the official start date but benefits require completed enrollment forms. If docs come later, coverage can be backdated to start date once verified, but this is admin-heavy. Recommend delaying 1 week for cleaner enrollment if employee prefers guaranteed coverage start.
Miguel (Payroll): For I-9: If employee is outside US on start date, we cannot complete section 2. There's a Dept. of Homeland Security allowance for remote hires using authorized agents in limited cases — but only for US-based remote. For overseas, we need a physical verification when she returns. Payroll can run pay as long as tax forms are submitted (W-4/ITIN discussions if needed).
Aisha (Recruiter): I spoke to Priya — she'd prefer to keep start date if benefits can be backdated. She doesn’t want more delays. She can sign forms digitally but understands I-9 will be done on return.
Immigration-Counsel-Bot: Counsel also suggests documenting remote-work agreement and a signed attestation that employee is not present in US for I-9 completion. Also recommend advising employee about re-entry risk and carry employer support letter (we can provide).
Sofia (People Ops): Action items: @Kunal — can you confirm benefit backdating and any blackout windows (enrollment deadlines)? @Miguel — confirm payroll will run and note any tax paperwork flags for remote start. @Immigration-Counsel-Bot — can you draft a short travel advisory we can share with Priya?
Kunal (Benefits): I’ll confirm by EOD. In general we can backdate enrollment to start date if forms are completed within the 30-day window; COBRA/eligibility implications minimal for single hire.
Miguel (Payroll): Payroll OK to pay if W-4 submitted and bank details provided. If she’s outside US >183 days there may be tax residency considerations — unlikely for a 10-day trip. I'll prepare a checklist for tax docs.
Immigration-Counsel-Bot: Draft below, feel free to edit before sending to candidate:
```
Hi Priya — quick travel advisory from Redwood immigration counsel:
- Travel while on OPT carries re-entry risk depending on visa stamping status.
- Carry your OPT EAD card, I-20 with travel signature, employment offer letter, and contact info for Redwood HR.
- If you’ll miss start date, we can backdate benefits if paperwork is completed within 30 days; I-9 must be completed in person after return.
- If you anticipate any delays >2 weeks, notify us and we’ll discuss premium filing options.
Regards,
Redwood Immigration Counsel
```
Alex (Hiring Manager): That looks good — can we also add a line saying the team will provide a loaner laptop and VPN access on day 1?
Sofia (People Ops): Good call. I’ll update and send. For the thread: unless Kunal/Miguel flag a blocker, we’ll proceed with start date unchanged and remote onboarding. Priya to confirm travel dates and sign digital forms.
Aisha (Recruiter): I’ll send the updated advisory and an onboarding checklist to Priya now and loop back here with her confirmation. :thumbsup:
Sofia (People Ops): Thanks everyone — please post any blockers in this thread.
Alex (Hiring Manager): Thanks team — appreciate the fast turnaround.
Miguel (Payroll): I'll add payroll checklist to the onboarding packet and DM Aisha the bank form link.
Kunal (Benefits): Sending benefit enrollment link now.
Sofia (People Ops): Thread follow-up: Priya confirmed travel 3/30–4/5, wants to keep 4/1 start. We’ll proceed with remote start and in-person I-9 on 4/6. Closing for now unless anything changes. :white_check_mark:
file_note: generated for immigration coordination scenario with OPT travel; unique phrasing compared to existing docs
